title: Actor

provenance.description: first-party: its code is in this repository (see the components that run in it). third-party: external software or a service the system depends on. ambient: provided by the platform or environment the system runs in (OS services, the user's shell).

kind.description: person: a human using or operating the system. program: a process on some machine (a CLI, an agent, a browser page, a daemon). service: something reached over a network that the system does not run itself, or runs as a managed deployment.

location.description: local: the user's machine. browser: a web page. remote: a server or machine the system operates itself. cloud: a managed service.

provider.description: Who runs it, for remote and cloud actors (Cloudflare, AWS, GitHub, …).

platform.description: The runtime or product: macOS LaunchAgent, Workers, Durable Objects, Node.js, …

talksTo.description: Ids of the actors this one communicates with, in either direction: the system's connection map, sketched before flows and protocols describe how.

description: Something with a runtime identity that takes part in the system's behaviour: a person or program that uses it, a process or service it runs, or one it calls. Code units are components, not actors.
